method_steps.action: Define operational capabilities, detail them with interacting operational activities, and allocate activities to operational entities.

outputs: Operational capabilities, activities, interactions, entities, and operational architecture views
method_steps.decision_rules: Decide which stakeholder activities belong to each operational entity.
method_steps.quality_or_exit_checks: Run model validation to find unallocated activities and other inconsistencies.
method_steps.branching_iteration_or_rework: Add missing stakeholders or relationships and revisit affected views when validation reveals omissions.

method_steps.action: Validate the operational model, correct allocation problems, and iterate all affected views.
material_inputs: Operational architecture and Capella validation messages
outputs: Corrected operational model and a ground-station-operator actor discovered from an unallocated activity
method_steps.automation: Capella reports validation warnings. Corrections are manual.
method_steps.decision_rules: Add a missing actor when an operational activity cannot be allocated to the existing actors.
method_steps.quality_or_exit_checks: Repeat validation until remaining warnings concern transitions to the next modeling phase.
method_steps.branching_iteration_or_rework: Any added element triggers review and update of related diagrams.

method_steps.action: Transition to system analysis, decide whether each operational activity is performed by the system or an external actor, decompose functions, create architecture and scenarios, and define functional chains.
material_inputs: Validated operational model and system boundary decisions
outputs: System functions, actors, architecture, scenarios, states, modes, exchanges, and functional chains
method_steps.automation: Capella can initialize or update some diagrams, while the modeler performs decomposition and allocation.
method_steps.decision_rules: Allocate an activity to the system when the system performs it. Otherwise allocate it to an external actor. Decompose partially performed activities until allocation is possible.
method_steps.quality_or_exit_checks: Validate the model and correct port or allocation warnings.
method_steps.branching_iteration_or_rework: Iterate architecture, states, functions, and exchanges when a new actor or transition is needed.

method_steps.action: Build the logical architecture by decomposing system functions, creating logical components, and allocating functions, exchanges, and ports.
material_inputs: System analysis model and required logical decomposition
outputs: Logical function breakdown, logical architecture, filtered views, and logical exchange scenario
method_steps.automation: Manual decomposition and allocation with Capella view generation and filtering.
method_steps.decision_rules: Use filters when the complete logical architecture is too complex for its audience.
method_steps.quality_or_exit_checks: Confirm functions, component exchanges, ports, and exchange items are allocated.
method_steps.branching_iteration_or_rework: Return to earlier views when logical decomposition exposes missing content.

method_steps.action: Transition to physical architecture, decompose logical functions, create physical nodes and behavior components, and allocate physical functions and interfaces.
outputs: Physical function breakdown, physical architecture, physical components, interfaces, and verification chains
method_steps.automation: Capella supports transitions and validation. Physical decomposition and allocation are manual.
method_steps.decision_rules: Transform logical components into physical nodes in this case and decompose functions until they can be allocated to behavior components.
method_steps.quality_or_exit_checks: Perform physical architecture validation after completing the diagram.
method_steps.branching_iteration_or_rework: Revise higher abstraction layers from top to bottom when physical modeling reveals an inconsistency.

method_steps.action: Validate and review the physical model from several viewpoints, correct the EPS deploy-signal allocation from the logical layer, and produce audience-specific final views.
material_inputs: Physical architecture, validation output, CubeSat deployment constraint, and stakeholder viewpoint needs
outputs: Corrected final physical architecture and filtered EPS-linked verification-chain views
method_steps.automation: Tool validation reports issues. Review, correction, and filter selection are manual.
method_steps.decision_rules: A deploy signal must not trigger power storage or activation in a way that violates the required post-deployment delay.
method_steps.quality_or_exit_checks: Correct inconsistencies and inspect the final Deploy Antennas and Obtain Housekeeping functional chains.
method_steps.branching_iteration_or_rework: Apply a physical finding to the logical architecture, then update lower views again.

branching_and_iteration.value: The process is explicitly iterative and incremental. Discoveries in one diagram complete or correct others, additions trigger review of related views, and physical findings can require correction from the logical layer downward.

completion_conditions.value: The modeled layer is validated, material inconsistencies are corrected, required allocations and realization links are addressed, and final architecture and verification-chain views are produced for the intended audience.

branching_and_iteration.value: Validation findings and newly discovered elements trigger iteration and updates across related or higher abstraction views.

citations.quote: The main purpose of this work is to present a conceptual framework that provides product related inputs for satellites AIT planning using MBSE during system design.

The framework application is demonstrated in the AIT of a university small satellite. The proposed framework showed that it promotes the contribution of the AIT team to product design, while captures in models approximately 91% of product related inputs that form the basis of AIT planning.
AIT engineers often inherit a finalized design, being required to deal during AIT with problems that could have been avoided had their perspective been included in the design process.
The AIT process is traditionally document-centric, and involves a large amount of documents.
This work is based on satellite AIT planning inputs, and proposes a conceptual framework to early involve AIT engineers and achieve part of these inputs on early project phases through MBSE.
Development of a conceptual framework that capture these inputs for AIT planning while product models are being developed;

Therefore, the results described herein were captured in a wide variety of standards (ECSS, 2009; 2012; NASA, 2007; ISO, 2011), real projects documentations (2004a-b; 2005a-c; 2006a; 2008a-b; 2009a-b; 2010a; 2011a-e; 2014a; 2015a-b) and specialists (from LIT/INPE) interviews.
The conceptual framework should provide a general recipe that will be handed to other practitioners to define AIT for their satellite systems.

The challenge here is to provide guidelines sufficiently flexible that it applies to a range of satellite systems (small and medium sizes) and modeling methods, yet not so broad that it becomes impractical.

The modeling process is intrinsically iterative and incremental. The different types of diagrams allow the subject to be tackled from other viewpoints: concepts discovered in one diagram allow others to be completed.
Beyond the iterative and incremental characteristics of modeling, it is also a process to be made by multiple specialists.

The first step is to define high-level objectives (Operational Capabilities, Figure 0.1). These Capabilities shall be detailed with Operational Activities that exchange Interactions. Then, the analysis will be completed with the allocation of the Operational Activities to Operational Entities (Figure 0.3).

The model shall be then validated to find modeling inconsistencies (Figures 0.4 and 0.5). After finding and correcting problems, operational activities shall be allocated to structural elements, which in Operational Analysis are called Operational Entities or Actors.

After this step, the analysis of the resulted model together with the unallocated operational activity (Obtain cubesat housekeeping data) evidenced the lack of a new stakeholder (ground station operator), that was not identified in first place.
Adding new elements brings the need of reviewing the other models to check for elements and relations inconsistencies. This shows the iterative characteristic of modelling.
The modeler shall identify if each operational activity from previous phase will be performed by the system to be developed or not (Figure 0.11).
The model shall be validated to expose modeling inconsistencies (Figure 0.16).
A Functional Chain is an important feature that guides future verification and validation tasks (Figure 0.18). It may be seen as a kind of verification path in the global data flow.

In order to define all exchanges of the system, it is created a class diagram. After that, each functional exchange and its ports shall have at least one exchange item defined in this diagram (e.g. current, temperature or voltage).
Then, all these functions are allocated to logical system components, and all functional exchanges, component exchanges and ports are set (Figure 0.31).
The physical architecture layer of arcadia considers the creation of physical components within the system, thus such step involves the realization of several technological choices.
This decomposition in lower level functions will allow the proper allocation into physical behavior components (blue rectangles in PAB diagram).
After the diagram is completed, a physical architecture validation (Figure 0.38) is performed to correct possible inconsistencies.
The Figure 0.39 shows the example of an inconsistency found during physical components allocation, but the correction is made since logical layer (logical architecture blank).

The deploy signal, which turns-on the satellite was mistakenly linked to "store power", making the system to generate power and to be turned-on unintentionally with any kind of light source (CubeSats have a very strict requirement to turn-on only after a specific time from deployment).
It is the modelers' job to be sensitive about the audience need and knowledge, and work with the several filters to precisely adequate the information (fit to purpose).
